items.title: Bill Mays interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, December 5, 2025
items.q: I had recently heard Earl “Fatha” Hines and the Miles Davis band in San Francisco which completely flipped me and turned my head around and opened my ears.

ctx.x: Oh that’s fascinating. So can you compare that with your first gig when you were 15?

When I was 15 I got called by some, a father-son team. They both played the banjo and they needed a pianist for their gig at the Gay Nineties Pizza Parlor in Pleasant Hills, California. I was going to high school in the East Bay area. And I didn’t know very many tunes. I didn’t know much about jazz. I had recently heard Earl “Fatha” Hines and the Miles Davis band in San Francisco which completely flipped me and turned my head around and opened my ears. But what they did, they gave me a fake book and they said…

a cord, a clothesline cord. No tone to speak of but he had a good beat, and the two banjo players. That was my first professional gig and I think I kind of remember making ten bucks a night which was probably a lot of money in the late ‘50s.
